newsitem.title: GERMANY: Britain's Blair hopes for success in Amsterdam.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Blair hopes for success in Amsterdam.

text.p: British Prime Minister Tony Blair said on Friday he would work hard for an agreement at this month's European Union summit in Amsterdam, but officials said a British opt-out on border controls could pose problems.

"It is important that we get a successful conclusion at the Inter-governmental Conference in Amsterdam and we will work very hard on that," Blair told journalists after he was greeted by Chancellor Helmut Kohl in Bonn.
British officials said the biggest obstacle to be overcome in Amsterdam was obtaining cast-iron assurances that Britain would be able to retain control over its external borders.

Blair intended to tell Kohl of his worry that some EU governments did not fully appreciate how important this issue was to Britain as an island nation that has always jealously protected its frontiers.
"Of all the issues this is the most difficult one in the run-up to Amsterdam," one official said.

Blair would also ask for language in the EU employment chapter to put job creation at the top of the European agenda by making people more "employable", by improving skills and making labour markets more flexible, officials said.
Kohl greeted Blair warmly and said he appreciated the fact that the new prime minister had chosen Germany as his first destination for an official visit.
Both men said they hoped relations between the two countries would continue to be close and stressed their commitment to the enlargement of the European Union and NATO.
